chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rifa'ah and Hafs, said: We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed to walk to the House of God on foot. He said: Let him walk, but when he becomes weary, let him ride.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone vows to walk to the Kaaba but gets tired?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of ease (*taysir*) in fulfilling vows, ruling that a vow to walk to the Kaaba is valid but not absolute if physical hardship arises. This reflects the Shia juristic view that vows are binding but subject to the capacity of the vow-maker, preventing unnecessary hardship (*darar*) while maintaining the spirit of devotion. The ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding *nadhr*, prioritizing the completion of the act over rigid literalism when circumstances change.
